runs.question: Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
runs.answer:
[Turn 1 | session=ses_06b21f34effewnhLRVQZkylAdf] Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
Here are the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet on **20 June 2026** (UTC):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| **Total slots** | 7,200 (7,180 blocks, **20 missed**) |
| **Slot range** | 14,590,799 – 14,597,998 |
| **Arrival ms (min → fastest node)** | **141 ms** |
| **Arrival ms (median)** | **1,453 ms** |
| **Arrival ms (p95)** | **3,126 ms** |
| **Arrival ms (max → slowest first-seen)** | **5,249 ms** |
| **Avg nodes observing per block** | ~157 |

The data comes from `mainnet.fct_block_first_seen_by_node` in the `xatu-cbt` dataset (`clickhouse-refined` datasource). The `first_seen_arrival_ms` is the minimum `seen_slot_start_diff` across all nodes — i.e., how many milliseconds after the slot started the fastest-to-see node first observed that block.

The histogram shows the distribution of first-seen block arrival latencies (in ms) across ~7,180 mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026, with the bulk clustered around 1,000–2,000 ms and a long tail up to ~5,200 ms.
